content.text: **Finding: compliant.** The assignment provision in § (h) already contains the carve-outs our playbook seeks.

input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: The clause is mutual and gives AP the free-assignment carve-out the preferred position requires: AP may assign without Kubient's consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld." A full-text search returns no "change of control" language anywhere in the Agreement, and the termination provisions contain no Kubient right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control, so the walk-away triggers are absent. Two preferred sub-elements are missing but are not material enough to redline: there is no express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor, and the consent carve-out runs to both parties rather than being one-way in our favour (i.e., at least at the fallback "mutual right to assign to successors" position). The "non-transferable, non-assignable" wording in the § 2 Kubient License is a standard licence-scope limitation on the technology grant, not a restriction on assignment of the Agreement, which § (h) governs and which expressly binds and benefits "successors and permitted assigns."
